repository.commitState: Uncommitted task changes at verification; local-only, no browser run, build, push or deployment.

scope: Pure Node post-processing repair for smoothness reports. It corrects a false gap introduced by frame filtering after rollback. It does not change game, input, transport, audio or browser scheduling and does not establish a new performance result.

harness.scope: Tested window-integration revision before any later scheduler-probe integration; this identity is not silently updated when the harness changes.

implementation.body: Contiguous original sample indices [first F >= 180, first F >= limit). No SessionPhase or rewound-next filter is applied.
implementation.frontier: Use complete per-sample networkPacing[][5] (native PredictionFrontier = max(next,replayEnd)). If unavailable, use explicitly labelled observed next high-water only, nativeFrontierComplete=false and window.complete=false. Captures never selects a boundary.
implementation.closedProgress: Throughput and cumulative correction/resimulation/capture deltas use endpoint minus start. The terminal marker closes elapsed time and optional new-state gaps; its callback cost belongs to tail while the start callback cost belongs to body.
implementation.presentation: Top-level gap fields retain body-only renderer-submission/RAF timestamp semantics. window.formalWithEndBoundary adds terminal closure. New-state observations require increasing submission count and frontier, with next equal to the observed frontier.
implementation.retention: Original report samples remain untouched. Newly generated reports preserve the exact old calculation under legacySummary, add summaryMethod, and use the corrected helper under summary. Existing frozen reports are never rewritten.
implementation.incomplete: Missing start/end, missing native frontier, duplicate or invalid pacing data, and counter/frontier/time regression remain explicit. No closed throughput or endpoint counter delta is reported for an invalid epoch or unobserved terminal marker.
implementation.costs: window.segments partitions all sampled callback costs exactly once into startup, body and tail and also reports allObserved. Cross-boundary new-state intervals and observed silence to an endpoint without a new state remain visible.
implementation.phase: scenes remains a compatibility alias of sessionPhases. Both are SessionPhase, not internal MatchScene; non-Match phases are retained.
implementation.timing: callbackCompletionGapMs is post-native sampledAt between renderer submissions, not total observer callback return. None of these measurements is physical scanout or acoustic acceptance.
implementation.identity: The harness hashes smoothness-window.mjs before the run and checks the same hash before the success report.

runtime.environment: nig Windows workspace; no browser, build or CPU-throttle command

contracts: Tail rollback cannot re-enter the formal body or manufacture a callback gap.
Rollback below the lower frame bound, non-Match phases, native work and a real 120 ms new-state gap are retained.
Captures ahead of simulation never chooses boundaries; native F may exceed a current replay cursor.
Endpoint counters close progress, endpoint work stays in tail, and start work stays in body.
Unobserved terminal crossing is right-censored; closed throughput/counter delta are null.
Missing/partial native F uses only labelled next high-water and never claims complete native evidence.
Counter resets and native frontier regression remain invalid-epoch evidence.
No new endpoint renderer submission leaves the observed new-state silence visible.
Missing start, empty samples and malformed input cannot fabricate a complete formal window.
Frozen relay125 recalculation agrees with independent prior evidence; the exact legacy calculation and all raw bytes remain unchanged.

retainedInitialFailure.change: Fixed only that synthetic tail row to frontier=5 and present=5 while next rewinds to 4 and captures remains 13. Helper code and rejection rules were unchanged.
retainedInitialFailure.significance: This was a malformed regression fixture, not a game/performance failure; it is retained rather than hidden by the passing rerun.

Its 83.735 ms RAF and 99.180 ms renderer gaps joined non-adjacent observations. The old values remain visible in the frozen raw and legacySummary; they are not a newly observed callback stall.

consumers.limitation: Historical aggregators do not enforce the new summary schema. An A/B comparison must use the same schema and boundary definition, or explicitly use legacySummary. Missing/invalid/incomplete windows must not be treated as accepted performance by a consumer.

limits: The earlier genuine relay39 active roughly 1.4 second RAF wait is unrelated to this false-filter-gap repair and remains unresolved.

Only the already retained relay125 raw report was recomputed; no new throughput, deeper rollback speedup, CPU4 native-rAF smoothness, network reliability, audio continuity or direct-route acceptance follows.
The terminal marker is deliberately excluded from body cost but retained in tail and allObserved. Cumulative endpoint deltas therefore do not describe exactly the same callback-cost cohort.
Without complete native frontier evidence, the labelled next high-water view remains an observation, not proof of replayEnd or a new simulation epoch.
A summary complete flag concerns its measurement boundaries/evidence, not product smoothness acceptance.
